New Chairperson Leads 59th BdREN Board of Trustees Meeting

May 10

0

The 59th Meeting of the Board of Trustees of Bangladesh Research and Education Network was held successfully at the meeting room of the Chairman of University Grants Commission of Bangladesh on May 07, 2026.
The meeting marked the inaugural Board Meeting chaired by the Honorable Chairperson of BdREN, Professor Dr. Mamun Ahmed, following his assumption of office. During the meeting, the Chairperson also welcomed three newly appointed Trustee Members to the Board: Prof. Dr. Md. Ziaur Rahman Chowdhury, Honorable Vice-Chancellor of Sylhet Medical University; Prof. Dr. Mohammad Mashud, Vice-Chancellor of Khulna University of Engineering & Technology; and Prof. Dr. Muhammad Masroor Ali, Professor at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology. Prof. Dr. Md. Saidur Rahman, Vice-Chairperson of BdREN, also welcomed the newly appointed Chairman of UGC and Chairperson of BdREN, Prof. Dr. Mamun Ahmed.
The Board discussed contemporary operational issues of BdREN and explored strategic directions for strengthening BdREN’s role as a key national institution supporting the country’s education, research, and innovation initiatives.

BdREN Conducts Workshop on AI and Institutional Collaboration at KYAU

Apr 30

0

Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN) successfully organized a workshop titled "Enhancement of Collaboration and Use of Generative AI" today at the KYAMCH Auditorium of Khwaja Yunus Ali University (KYAU), with the active participation of 144 attendees and with the active support of the KYAU as well as KYAMC.

The workshop was orchestrated as part of BdREN’s ongoing efforts to strengthen collaboration among academic institutions and promote the effective use of emerging technologies, particularly generative AI, in higher education. The event brought together faculty members, officials, and stakeholders to explore innovative solutions for research, administration, and the learning environment.

The program began with registration and a welcome address by the Director of IQAC, followed by remarks from BdREN’s CEO, highlighting the organization’s commitment to advancing digital transformation across Bangladesh’s education and research network. The Honorable Vice Chancellor of KYAU attended as the Chief Guest, while the Principal of KYAMC joined as the Special Guest, reinforcing institutional support for the initiative.

BdREN experts led a series of technical sessions to showcase its service landscape, AI-driven tools, network security solutions, and e-Resource portfolio. A dedicated segment on AI-powered survey tools demonstrated practical applications that institutions can adopt to enhance efficiency and data-driven decision-making.

A key highlight of the workshop was the interactive discussion session on enhancing collaboration, where participants exchanged ideas and explored opportunities for future partnerships leveraging on BdREN networks: Physical, logical, and human.

The event concluded with a networking lunch, reaffirming BdREN’s role as a catalyst for innovation, collaboration, and technology adoption in Bangladesh’s higher education ecosystem.

BdREN Hosts “Meet & Greet 2026” to Strengthen University Collaboration

Apr 23

0

BdREN Hosts “Meet & Greet 2026”, a Service awareness workshop to enrich Research and Education Through strengthening Collaboration with Private Universities of Dhaka and around.

The Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN) successfully organized the “Meet & Greet 2026” on 23 April at the UGC Auditorium, aiming to enhance collaboration among UGC, BdREN, and private universities for the advancement of research and education in Bangladesh.

A total of 85 representatives from 41 private universities across Dhaka participated in the program, reflecting strong interest in building a connected and collaborative academic ecosystem. The event was chaired by BdREN’s Chief Executive Officer, Mohammad Tawrit, while the welcome speech was delivered by Chief Marketing Officer- Ekhlas Uddin Ahmed.

Professor Dr. Mohammad Anwar Hossen, Member of UGC, attended as the Chief Guest and highlighted the importance of BdREN’s services in ensuring global competitiveness in education. Special Guest Dr. Sultan Mahmud Bhuiyan, Director of the Private University Management Division, emphasized the need to strengthen research capacity in private universities.

Three distinguished representatives from private universities - Prof. Dr. Mostafa Mahmud Hasan, Dean, Faculty of Business, Khwaja Yunus Ali University; Prof. Khawza Iftekhar Uddin, Pro-VC, Green University of Bangladesh; and Dr. Md. Zahid Hossain Shoeb, Librarian, North South University, also spoke at the event. They expressed gratitude to BdREN and shared their expectations for deeper collaboration and easier access to eResources for research and academic development.

In his remarks, CEO Mohammad Tawrit reaffirmed BdREN’s commitment to expanding services across all universities. The program concluded with a shared vision of strengthening innovation, research excellence, and institutional collaboration nationwide.

BdREN Expands High-Speed Campus Network at CU New Arts Building

Apr 07

0

Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN) has successfully completed the campus network extension at the New Arts Building of the University of Chittagong (CU), marking a significant step forward in enhancing digital connectivity for higher education in Bangladesh.

The newly connected five-storied building consists of 30 blocks, accommodating 14 academic departments under one roof. Through this initiative, more than 10,000 students and over 250 faculty members now benefit from seamless, high-speed internet access designed to support modern teaching, learning, and research activities.

To ensure reliable and uninterrupted connectivity throughout the premises, BdREN deployed 144 centrally managed Wireless Access Points (WAPs), enabling consistent coverage across classrooms, laboratories, corridors, and faculty areas. The wired network infrastructure has also been strengthened with the installation of 27 access switches and 560 faceplates, ensuring stable and efficient connectivity for both academic and administrative use.

A high-capacity 10 Gigabit (10G) backbone has been implemented from core to access level, allowing the network to handle heavy data traffic and peak usage without compromising performance. Additionally, a centralized Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) system has been introduced, providing approximately 2.5 hours of backup power to maintain continuous network operations during power outages.

This project highlights BdREN’s ongoing commitment to building a robust, scalable, and future-ready digital ecosystem for educational institutions across Bangladesh, empowering students, educators, and researchers with the connectivity they need to excel in a digital-first world.

UGC Chairman Prof. Dr. Mamun Ahmed Visits BdREN Office, Provides Strategic Guidance

Apr 04

0

Prof. Dr. Mamun Ahmed, Chairman, UGC, and Chairperson, BdREN Trust, paid a visit to the BdREN Office today [04 April 2026] in the afternoon. Prof. Dr. Md. Saidur Rahman, Member, UGC and vice-Chairperson, BdREN Trust, Prof. Dr. Tanzimuddin Khan, Member, UGC and Member, BdREN Trust, and Dr. Fakhrul Islam, Secretary, UGC, accompanied the Honorable Chairperson during the visit. The high officials of BdREN warmly greeted the Chairperson.

After a brief introduction of all the attendees, the CEO of BdREN gave a presentation on the formation of BdREN Trust and its authority to formulate policies and drive the organization toward achieving its goals. He also highlighted the milestones achieved, BdREN’s service coverage, its financial sustainability, and opportunities and challenges. CEO, BdREN, solicited the guidance and advice of the Honorable Chairperson to overcome the challenges and make the organization stride ahead with aplomb.

The Honorable Chairperson opened the floor and collected comments from the other higher BdREN officials present in the meeting. Then, the Honorable Chairperson advised the CEO, BdREN, to run the organization specifically as a Business Unit to provide full support to the research and educational community. He threw some challenging targets for the BdREN officials to achieve. He requested the CEO, BdREN, to chalk out and submit a plan to meet those targets.

Prof. Tanzimuddin Khan stressed the need to promote BdREN services to the community, whereas Prof. Dr. Md. Saidur Rahman asked BdREN officials to work as a cohesive unit for the betterment of BdREN.

The meeting ended with the Honorable Chairperson thanking all officials for their active participation.

Call for Fellowship for APAN62, 10th- 14th August 2026, Auckland, New Zealand

Mar 10

0

Following the success of the APAN61 Fellowship Program, which selected 20 fellows from 10 economies, we are pleased to announce that the
APAN62 Fellowship Program is now open for applications
.
The
62nd APAN Meeting
will take place from
10th to 14th August 2026, in Auckland, New Zealand
.
Fellowship Details and Eligibility:
Full details on criteria and selection procedures are available at:
https://apan.net/fellowship/
Applications are encouraged from
graduate and undergraduate students
, as well as
young researchers
.
Applicants presenting at APAN62 will receive
priority consideration
. Please note that presenting at APAN62 requires a separate submission under the Call for Presentation Proposals (to be issued later).
Selection for fellowship does not guarantee acceptance as a presenter
— both processes are managed independently.
There will also be a conference component to APAN62. If you are interested in submitting a paper, you may do so here:
https://apanconf.apan.net/
(Closing: 15th April 2026)
Fellowship Coverage:
The fellowship includes:
Registration Fee
– Access to all sessions, workshops, and tutorials.
Food
– Lunch, tea during the conference, and two social dinners.
Per-Diem Allowances
– Covers airport-to-venue transport, breakfast, and remaining dinners. This may include a transport allowance from the international airport to accommodation (and vice versa) or other ground transportation and uncovered meals during the meeting.
Accommodation
– Twin-sharing / dormitory basis with breakfast during APAN62 (venue to be notified to successful applicants).
Important Airfare Requirements:
Airfare is NOT covered
under the fellowship program.
Applicants must provide
proof of airfare support
(from their institution/organisation or self-funded) at the time of application. Without this letter, applications will be immediately rejected.
If you are self-funding your airfare, you may be required to submit a
confirmed itinerary
upon fellowship acceptance.
We strongly advise checking flight availability and approvals
before applying
to avoid last-minute cancellations, which disrupt the selection process.
We are opening up the fellowship earlier than usual to facilitate Visa and Flight processing, so please be mindful if you are accepted into the fellowship of time sensitivity  in getting your necessary documents.
Attendance Commitment:
Fellows must be available for the
entire week of 10th – 14th August
, with attendance on the
first day being mandatory
.
Except during official APAN social events, fellows are responsible for their
own dinner expenses
.
Applicants with prior no-shows without notice will be
automatically rejected
under the
Blacklisting Policy
.
Application Submission:
Submit your application
HERE
. Additional details about the APAN Fellowship Program will also be posted on the event website later :
https://apan62.apan.net/

Important Dates:
What's Happening                                                                                                         Date

| Call for Fellowship (CFF) | 10th March 2026, Tuesday |
| --- | --- |
| CFF closes | 27th March 2026, Friday |
| Member Country Review | 6th – 17th April 2026 |
| Fellowship Committee Review | 22nd – 29th April 2026 |
| Announcement of Selection | 4th May 2026, Monday |
| Confirmation by Selected Fellows | 15th May 2026, Friday |


Should you have any enquiries before applying, please email us at
sec@apan.net
.

Both parties engaged in a fruitful discussion and expressed mutual interest in working collaboratively in the near future.

APAN61 Successfully Concludes in Dhaka

Jan 30

0

The 61st Asia Pacific Advanced Network (APAN61) Meeting concluded successfully today at Le Méridien Dhaka. The five-day international conference was jointly hosted by the Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN) and the HEAT Project, bringing together global researchers, academicians, and ICT professionals to advance collaboration in research and education networking.

The formal inauguration ceremony was held on 27 January 2026 at the Grand Ballroom of the hotel. The session was chaired by Prof. Dr. Md. Saidur Rahman, Member, University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh and Vice-Chairperson of BdREN. The opening address was delivered by Mr. Mohammad Tawrit, Chief Executive Officer of BdREN. Prof. Shinji Shimojo, Chairman of the Asia Pacific Advanced Network (APAN), attended the ceremony as the Chief Guest, while the closing remarks were delivered by Prof. Dr. Mohammad Tanzimuddin Khan, Member, UGC Bangladesh. The inauguration featured keynote addresses by Ms. Karin Wessel (SURF, Netherlands) on global research and education collaboration and Dr. Azreen Karim, Senior Research Fellow, BIDS, on economic perspectives in the Asia-Pacific region.

APAN61 hosted Working Group sessions, Special Interest Groups (SIGs), Birds of a Feather (BoF) meetings, training programs, and technical discussions focusing on advanced networking, cybersecurity, data sharing, emerging technologies, and regional cooperation. Cultural programs highlighting Bangladesh’s heritage were also part of the event.  The conference recorded 355 participants from 20 countries, with both onsite and virtual attendance. A total of 101 speakers, 35 organizers, and 17 sponsors contributed to the successful execution of the event. As the national research and education network of Bangladesh, BdREN is honored to host APAN61, reaffirming its commitment to strengthening global partnerships and advancing digital connectivity for research and education.

The summit officially concluded with a formal handover ceremony, reaffirming a continued commitment to regional collaboration in research and digital infrastructure.

text:
BdREN Showcases Expertise at bdNOG 20, Empowering the Nation's Digital Ecosystem

Nov 15

0

The recent bdNOG 20 conference served as a dynamic platform for networking, knowledge sharing, and technological advancement, and BdREN was at the heart of the action.A team of our skilled engineers attended the event as trainer to lead a 3-day hands-on training program and also presented a critical case study about BdREN’s recent innovative development in cloud system. In addition to those active participations, we have sponsored to this prestigious event, which continues the manifestation of BdREN-BdNOG collaboration.

The engagement began with a comprehensive
3-day workshop on "Virtualization with Proxmox VE,"
focusing on building an enterprise-level private cloud, which was meticulously designed and conducted by our BdREN expert.
Khandakar Rashedul Arefin
and
Jamilur Rahman
conducted the whole training sessions. As digital infrastructure becomes increasingly complex, the ability to efficiently manage compute resources is paramount. This hands-on session provided participants from various Industries like ISP, Banks, NTTN etc. with the practical skills needed to deploy and manage a robust, open-source virtualization environment using ProxMox.

Participants delved into the core concepts of virtualization, learning how to manage virtual machines and containers, deploy software-defined storage (SDS) using Ceph, build Hyper-converged Infrastructure (HCI) and establish secure & resilient infrastructure. The workshop was highly interactive, with attendees solving real-world scenarios, which equipped them to optimize their own institutional IT resources, reduce costs, and enhance service delivery. The overwhelming positive feedback highlighted the workshop's value in building critical local capacity.

Forms response chart. Question title: Rate your knowledge and capacity development from this Training
. Number of responses: 19 responses.

Following the workshop, BdREN took the main conference stage to present a compelling
case study on "Application Load Balancing using Kubernetes HPA."
As modern applications evolve to be more complex and demand high availability, efficient load balancing has become a cornerstone of reliable digital services.

Our presentation walked the audience through a real-world implementation, detailing how Kubernetes' native and advanced load-balancing capabilities can be leveraged to ensure seamless user experience, distribute traffic efficiently, and maintain application resilience even during peak loads or partial system failures. The case study provided invaluable insights for developers, system administrators, and network engineers looking to build scalable and fault-tolerant applications in a cloud-native world.

This dual contribution at bdNOG 20—from laying the foundational bricks of virtualization to demonstrating the advanced orchestration of containerized applications—perfectly encapsulates BdREN's mission. We are not just a network service provider; we are a catalyst for growth and innovation.

By sharing knowledge and pioneering solutions, we are actively strengthening the backbone of Bangladesh's digital landscape, one workshop and one case study at a time.

HEAT Project in collaboration with the BdREN Organizes Two-Day Workshop to align beneficiary institutions with project's strategic goals

Nov 03

0

Gazipur, October 20-21, 2025
– The Higher Education Acceleration and Transformation (HEAT) Project, in collaboration with the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh (UGC) and Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN), successfully organized a two-day residential workshop at Sarah Resort Ltd., Rajabari, Rajendrapur, Sreepur, Gazipur on October 20-21, 2025. The workshop brought together ICT and IICT Heads/Directors from universities across Bangladesh to align beneficiary institutions with HEAT project's strategic goals, particularly focusing on IT infrastructure, ICT development, and campus network enhancement plans. Participants departed from UGC at 8:00 AM on the first day, reaching the resort around 9:30 AM to begin an intensive two-day program of presentations, discussions, and hands-on technical demonstrations.
The first day centered on "Aligning the Beneficiaries with the Project Deliverables," with Professor Dr. Asaduzzaman (Project Director, HEAT) delivering the keynote presentation, supported by addresses from Professor Khurshid Alam (Deputy Project Director), Professor Salina Zaman (Chief Program Co-Ordinator), Professor Dr. Mohammed Shafiul Alam Khan (Wing Manager and BdREN Technical Specialist), and Mohammad Tawrit (CEO, BdREN). ICT Directors from Dhaka University, Shahjalal University of Science and Technology, Bangladesh Agricultural University, and Patuakhali Science and Technology University presented their current ICT infrastructure situations, limitations, and challenges, fostering productive discussions about implementation strategies. The second day focused on "Advanced Labs Without Walls," featuring keynote and demonstrations by BdREN's Khandakar Rashedul Arefin (General Manager, Systems & Services), Jamilur Rahman (Manager, Systems & Cloud), and Abu Naser Md. Nafew (Manager, Innovation) on Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) and AI Infrastructure. The hands-on session allowed university ICT directors to experience cloud-based laboratory solutions firsthand, demonstrating how institutions can provide world-class computing facilities to students and researchers without extensive physical infrastructure investments.
This comprehensive two-day workshop successfully achieved its objectives of familiarizing university ICT leadership with HEAT project deliverables and demonstrating innovative solutions for modern educational infrastructure. The combination of strategic alignment discussions, knowledge sharing about ground realities, and hands-on experience with advanced technologies created a strong foundation for effective project implementation across beneficiary institutions.

BdREN conducts “Generative AI for Productivity & Innovation” workshop for UGC officials

Oct 27

0

Dhaka, 23 October 2025— The University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh hosted the opening of BdREN’s two-day training workshop “
Generative AI for Productivity & Innovation
” delivered in two batches on 15–16 October and 22–23 October 2025 at UGC Bhaban, Dhaka. Professor Dr. Md. Saidur Rahman, Member, UGC, attended as Chief Guest, with Dr. Md. Fakhrul Islam, Secretary, UGC, as Special Guest; Md. Omar Faruque, Director, ICT Division, UGC, presided over the session, and Muhammad Nazmul Islam, Additional Director, ICT Division, UGC, delivered the welcome address.
The sessions were led by Khandakar Rashedul Arefin, General Manager (Systems & Services), BdREN, and Abu Naser Md. Nafew, Manager (Innovation), BdREN.
Designed specifically for UGC officials, the program covered core GenAI concepts, prompt engineering (with hands-on use of the CRAFT framework and related methods), and practical applications for official communication, report and presentation development, research/data analysis, and department-wise solution design. The curriculum was structured over two days—Day 1: Foundation & Core Application (demystifying GenAI, mastering prompts, GenAI for effective communication, and supercharging document creation) and Day 2: Advanced Applications & Strategic Implementation (GenAI for research and analysis, department-specific brainstorming labs, solution presentation/feedback, and the way forward)—with an explicit mandate to empower UGC officials for the digital future.
Building on UGC’s operational needs, the workshop emphasized measurable benefits for government higher-education administration including streamlined reporting, enhanced official communication, faster data sense-making, Bangla–English translation support, and time savings on routine documentation so participants can apply GenAI responsibly to improve daily workflows and policy support functions.
Participants were highly enthusiastic throughout and requested additional training, including advanced tracks tailored to specific roles and use cases.

text:
Call for Fellowship for APAN61, 26th January - 30th January 2026, Dhaka, Bangladesh

Sep 29

0

| Call for Fellowship (CFF) | 17th September 2025. Wednesday |
| --- | --- |
| CFF Closes | 7th October 2025, Tuesday |
| Member Country Review | 2nd-12th October 2025 |
| Fellowship Committee Review | 13th – 15th October 2025 |
| Announcement of Selection | 16th October 2025, Thursday |
| Confirmation by Selected Fellows | 24th October 2025, Wednesday |

Overview
The APAN Fellowship Program offers a unique platform for students and early-career researchers to engage in the Asia Pacific Advanced Network (APAN) meetings. Building on the success of the APAN60 Fellowship Program, which welcomed 18 fellows from 14 economies, we are pleased to announce that applications are now open for the APAN61 Fellowship Program. The 61st APAN Meeting will be hosted from
26–30 January 2026 in Dhaka, Bangladesh
.

Fellowship Details and Eligibility
· Full details on criteria and selection procedures are available at:
https://apan.net/fellowship/
· Applications are encouraged from
graduate and undergraduate
students, as well as
young researchers
.
· Applicants presenting at APAN61 will receive
priority consideration
. Please note that presenting at APAN61 requires a separate submission under the Call for Presentation Proposals (to be issued later).
Selection for fellowship does not guarantee acceptance as a presenter
— both processes are managed independently.

Fellowship Coverage
The fellowship includes:
·
Registration Fee
– Access to all sessions, workshops, and tutorials.
·
Food
– Lunch, tea during the conference, and two social dinners.
·
Per-Diem Allowances
– Covers airport-to-venue transport, breakfast, and remaining dinners. This may include a transport allowance from the international airport to accommodation (and vice versa) or other ground transportation and uncovered meals during the meeting.
·
Accommodation
– Twin-sharing basis with breakfast during APAN61 (venue to be notified to successful applicants).
If you plan to arrange your own accommodation at your own cost, you must notify the APAN Secretariat at least one month in advance to avoid non-refund of the accommodation allowance. Please do not request a single room or specific roommates, or make independent bookings without notification, as this disrupts planning.

Important Airfare Requirements
· Airfare is NOT covered under the fellowship program.
· Applicants must provide proof of airfare support (from their institution/organisation or self-funded) at the time of application. Without this letter, applications will be immediately rejected.
· If you are self-funding your airfare, you may be required to submit a confirmed itinerary upon fellowship acceptance.
· We strongly advise checking flight availability and approvals before applying to avoid last-minute cancellations, which disrupt the selection process.

Attendance Commitment
· Fellows must be available for the entire week of 26–30 January 2026, with attendance on the first day being mandatory.
· Except during official APAN social events, fellows are responsible for their own dinner expenses.
· Applicants with prior no-shows without notice will be automatically rejected under the Blacklisting Policy.

text:
BdREN & UGC organized Workshop on e-Resources

Jul 03

0

Dhaka, July 2, 2025 —
The Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN), in collaboration with the ICT Division and the University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh, successfully organized the
“Workshop on e-Resources”
today at Hotel Lakeshore Heights, Dhaka.
The event was graced by
Professor Dr. SMA Faiz
, Hon’ble Chairman of UGC and Chairperson of BdREN Trust, as the Chief Guest. The workshop was inaugurated by
Dr. Md. Fakhrul Islam
, Hon’ble Secretary of UGC, who added significance to the event with his valued presence and insights.
Mr. Md. Rezaul Karim Hawlader
, Director (Finance & Accounts), UGC, also actively participated in the workshop.
Treasurers, librarians, comptrollers, and Directors (Finance and Accounts) from various public and private universities participated actively. Officials from UGC and the ICSETP & HEAT projects were also present, reflecting the importance of a unified national effort toward equitable access to academic e-resources.
The workshop focused on developing a rational and sustainable
subscription model
for availing e-books and e-journals in higher education institutions.
Professor Dr. Abdullah Shams Bin Tariq
, Convener of the Subscription Model Framing Committee, presented the proposed model, followed by engaging group discussions and structured feedback sessions.
The event concluded with advisory remarks from the Chief Guest, who commended BdREN’s efforts to strengthen the digital resource infrastructure in higher education. He also emphasized the importance of collaboration among stakeholders to ensure long-term sustainability.
Mr. Md. Omar Faruque
, Director, ICT Division, UGC, delivered a vote of thanks to the participants.
Both UGC and BdREN reiterated their expectations of full cooperation from all universities to make quality e-resources accessible to students and faculty across Bangladesh.

ERP intiatives for Automation of Universities and UGC Operations

May 22

0

In a major move towards digital transformation in higher education, the University Grants Commission (UGC) of Bangladesh has taken the initiative to bring all operations of UGC and the country's universities under a unified automation system through the development of an integrated ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) software.
The announcement was made at a day-long workshop titled
"Expert Opinion on UGC-ERP Software Architecture and Design"
held at the UGC auditorium on May 19, 2025. The ERP software will be developed under the Higher Education Acceleration and Transformation (HEAT) Project and is expected to streamline and automate academic, research, accreditation, project proposals, financial management, and institutional profiling activities across UGC and universities.
Professor Dr. S.M.A. Faiz, Chairman of UGC, graced the workshop as the Chief Guest. The session was presided over by UGC Member Professor Dr. Md. Saidur Rahman, while UGC Member Professor Dr. Mohammad Tanzimuddin Khan attended as the Special Guest. Other distinguished speakers included UGC Secretary Dr. Md. Fakhrul Islam, ICT Director Md. Omar Faruque, HEAT Project Director Professor Dr. Asaduzzaman, and Mohammad Towrit, CEO- BdREN.
BdREN, as a key stakeholder in the digital transformation of Bangladesh's higher education ecosystem, reaffirms its commitment to supporting this landmark initiative, which aligns with its mission to enhance ICT infrastructure and services across academia.

text:
Call for Fellowship (CFF) at APAN 60

Mar 30

0

The APAN59 Fellowship Program was a success with 29 fellows from 9 economies selected. With that, the APAN 60 Fellowship Program is
now open for applications
. The 60th APAN Meeting will be held from
28th July – 1st August 2025 in Grand Hyatt, Hong Kong
Please see
https://apan.net/fellowship/
for more details about the Fellowship Criteria and Selection Procedure.
Students (graduates and undergraduates) are encouraged to apply for fellowships although other young researchers may also be considered. Applicants who are presenting at the APAN 60 will be given precedence. If you have plans of presenting, please submit your proposal in the Call for Presentation Proposals that will be sent out after this call.
The Fellowship Program fund covers the following: (Please read the below points as it’s crucial for your application)
1. Registration Fee: Access to All Sessions/Workshops/Tutorials
2. Food: Lunch and Tea (During Conferences) and 2 Social Dinners
3. Per-Diem allowances (Airport-Venue-Airport transport, Breakfast and Remaining Dinner) : Transport Allowance (if applicable) (From International Airport to the accommodation site and vice versa) or any other ground transportation to the venue and meals that are not covered during the APAN meeting.
4.
Accommodation with no breakfast on twin sharing basis during APAN 60 (Venue will be notified to successful applicants). Should you wish to arrange your accommodation (at your own cost) please notify the APAN SEC a month before the event to avoid non-refund of accommodation allowance. Please do not request for single room or to be roomed with your fellow country mate, or book on your own without notifying us as it disrupts our planning.
Please note that the applicants must ensure the AVAILABILITY of their airfare (please check your airfare and accessibility to Hong Kong before applying, as airfare is NOT covered under the fellowship. You are required to provide a letter of proof for the support for airfare from your institution/organization or yourself. Do note without this letter, your application will be immediately rejected.
In cases where you bear the airfare personally, you may be required to provide a confirmed itinerary at the time of acceptance of the Fellowship.
Except for the occasions of APAN social events, the fellows are expected to plan their dinner expenses on their own.
Please also ensure you do not have any work commitments for this one week as you are required to be in attendance the whole week beginning 28th July 2025. Being present on the first day is crucial. For those who have applied for the APAN fellowship earlier and appeared as no show without notice will also be automatically rejected (Please refer to Blacklisting policy :
https://apan.net/fellowship/
)
Please submit your application
HERE
and details of the fellowship program will also be available on the event website later (
APAN Fellowship Program – Asia Pacific Advanced Network
)

BdREN to Host Network Automation Training with APNIC at Cox’s Bazar

Mar 27

0

BdREN is proud to announce a comprehensive training program on “Network Automation” scheduled to be held from 20–24 April 2025 at the Sea Pearl Beach Resort & Spa, Cox’s Bazar.

This five-day hands-on training is being organized in collaboration with APNIC, the Asia Pacific Network Information Centre, renowned for its global expertise in internet infrastructure and capacity building. The training will focus on empowering participants with modern network automation tools and techniques to enhance efficiency, reliability, and scalability in managing institutional networks.

The training will bring together 40 participants from across the Asia-Pacific region, including 22 participants from Bangladesh, 6 each from Sri Lanka, Pakistan, and Nepal. The course will be led by two seasoned trainers from APNIC, who will cover a range of topics including configuration management, automation workflows, and practical use of tools like Ansible and Git for network operations.

This initiative is part of BdREN’s continuous effort to build technical capacity among member institutions and support the digital transformation of the education and research community in Bangladesh. The training will be jointly financed by Asi@Connect Projet and BdREN.

Stay tuned for updates and insights from the training!

BdREN Mourns the Loss of Its Former Chairperson, Prof. Dr. Kazi Shahidullah

Mar 19

0

It is with deep sorrow and heavy hearts that we announce the passing of Prof. Dr. Kazi Shahidullah, former Chairman of the University Grants Commission (UGC) and ex-Chairperson of BdREN, who left us today (Wednesday) afternoon suffering from deadly cancer.

Prof. Dr. Shahidullah was a beacon of integrity, honesty, and wisdom. His contributions to the development and successes of BdREN during his reign of incumbency for a period of more than 4 years are immeasurable. He served BdREN with unwavering commitment, guiding it to greater heights before stepping down in August-2024 due to illness. His leadership, vision, and determination have left an unforgettable mark on the education and research landscape in Bangladesh.

Despite his long battle with chronic illness, his spirit remained unbroken, and he continued to inspire all who worked alongside him. Prof. Shahidullah was a true statue of righteousness, and his legacy of service to education will live on in the hearts and minds of many.

We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, colleagues, and all who had the privilege of working with him. May his soul rest in peace.

text:
BdREN Delegation Shines at APAN 59 in Japan

Mar 19

0

A BdREN delegation attended the 59th biannual Conference of APAN in Yokohama, Japan from March 03 to March 08, 2025. The delegation was led by Prof. Dr. S M A Faiz, Chairman of UGC and Chairperson of BdREN, and included representatives from its core team. The team actively participated in high-level discussions, technical presentations, and strategic networking sessions. In addition to that two fellows Md. Rayhan of Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University and S N Shayokh of Gazipur Agricultural University participated the event from the member institutes of BdREN.
The Honourable Chairman, who participated the event as BdREN’s Governor to Asi@Connect project, attended the Asi@Connect Governors’ Meeting and stamped his presence with remarks about his optimism on the planned second phase of Asi@Connect project and his commitment on behalf of BdREN to make the next phase of Asi@Connect successful.
Mohammad Tawrit, Chief Executive Officer, BdREN led a panel discussion session on “Internet Governance”. The topic of this session was “NRENs’ role in shielding Internet Fragmentation”. The panellists in this session were from BdREN, Tsinghua University, LEARN, NREN, PERN and KISTI. Various Acts and Policies contributing to Internet Fragmentation in respective countries were presented and rigorous analysis and discussion followed. Also, audience actively participated in the question and answering session. The session ended up with some resolution on containing Internet Fragmentation targeting APAN60 and APAN61.
Chief Executive Officer of BdREN, also chaired two back-to-back sessions on collaborations of emerging NRENs in Asia-Pacific region. In these sessions various NRENs came up with the recent updates of their network and services and also with their future plans. Nafew of BdREN made a demonstration on FileSender Application developed by BdREN in collaboration with APAN. Arefin, BdREN and Rajan from NREN came up with eduroam usage in the airports of the respective countries. In the second session the planned activities of next phase of Asi@Connect were discussed and a survey was conducted to figure out the priority of planned services.
Md. Ariful Islam, Manager (Data & Transmission), showcased BdREN’s BGPWatch platform, a real-time network monitoring tool, while Kh. Rashedul Arefin, Manager (Data Center), outlined BdREN’s future initiatives to enhance research connectivity.
Dr. Mohammad Farooq Ali Tarafder, FCMA, ACS, CAFO of BdREN, attended the TEIN Governors Meeting as a steering committee member. He particularly focused on expanding BdREN’s integration with Asia-Pacific research networks. Mohammad Tawrit, CEO, BdREN was also present in the Governors’ Meeting as a special request from TEIN*CC to contribute on the planning of next phase of Asi@Connect.
BdREN officials Arefin took part in the AP-GAINED Workshop, facilitated by LEARN, as an instructor contributing to knowledge-sharing and regional capacity-building efforts. Khadizatul Kubra and Abu Naser Md. Nafew from BdREN joined the same workshop as fellows.
It was a wonderful opportunity for BdREN officials to discuss the issues, challenges and opportunities with the NREN representatives from different countries, APAN officials, and service providers from ORCID, Inspera, as well as representatives from GEANT during side meetings. Many ideas came out to grab certain opportunities and to overcome the existing challenges.
BdREN’s engagement at APAN59 reinforced its role in shaping up digital innovation and connectivity in Bangladesh as well as in the Asia-Pacific region. The delegation returned with key takeaways to further develop next-generation network solutions, particularly focusing on gearing up activities revolving around federation, governance of internet and artificial intelligence.

and

.
This collaboration marks another milestone in BdREN's mission to

, ensuring that institutions like BSMRMU have access to world-class digital infrastructure and connectivity.

BdREN proudly sponsored the 4th International Conference on Electrical, Computer, and Communication Engineering (ECCE 2025), held from February 13-15, 2025, at Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), Chattogram, Bangladesh. Organized by the Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering, CUET, the event brought together researchers, academics, and industry experts from across the globe. BdREN's sponsorship reaffirmed its commitment to fostering innovation and research in engineering and technology. Representing BdREN, CTO Ekhlas Uddin Ahmed reiterated BdREN's role in enhancing Bangladesh's research and education sector, highlighting CUET's significance in this mission. He emphasized the impact of the HEAT project, which aims to strengthen digital infrastructure and academic research facilities. He also encouraged young researchers to explore emerging technologies like Artificial Intelligence, IoT, and Big Data Analytics, leveraging the potential of the 4th Industrial Revolution. The conference fostered valuable networking opportunities, reinforcing BdREN's dedication to supporting initiatives that drive the growth of research and education in Bangladesh.

AP-GAINED Pilot Training on Generative AI Successfully Concludes at BdREN

Feb 13

0

The three-day international "Pilot Training Workshop on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI)" concluded on a high note at the BdREN Training Room on Wednesday, February 12, 2025. The training, held from February 10–12, 2025, was organized by BdREN under the Asia Pacific – Generative AI Integration for NREN Empowerment and Development (AP-GAINED) project and conducted by two expert instructors from the Lanka Education and Research Network (LEARN).
AP-GAINED is an innovative initiative led by LEARN and supported by the APNIC Foundation through the ISIF Asia Fund. The project aims to enhance the capabilities of National Research and Education Network (NREN) professionals by equipping them with Generative AI skills, fostering innovation, and improving operational efficiency across the Asia Pacific region.
Designed for both technical and non-technical staff, the training provided practical, hands-on experience with Generative AI tools, benefiting professionals from IT, administration, finance, communications, marketing, and related fields. As mentioned more than 35 professionals from technical, administrative, finance and other associated departments of both BdREN and University Grants Commission of Bangladesh (UGC) participated in the training program. Participants engaged in interactive sessions, discussions, and hands-on activities to explore how GenAI can enhance day-to-day operations.
During the closing ceremony, the two trainers, Prof. Dr. Roshan G. Ragel, Consultant (CEO) of LEARN, and Dr. Asitha Bandaranayake, Consultant (CTO) of LEARN distributed certificates to the participants. Khandakar Rashedul Arefin, Manager, BdREN and Abu Naser Md. Nafew, Network Engineer, BdREN assisted the two overseas instructors in conducting the training program. The training brought together network engineers, software programmers, and administrative staff from Finance, Accounts, HR, and Procurement, representing UGC and BdREN.
The workshop served as an invaluable platform for sharing knowledge and best practices in integrating Generative AI into daily operations. As the event concluded, participants departed with enhanced skills and strategies to strengthen their institutions' digital frameworks through AI-driven solutions.

text:
Team BdREN Visits University of Chittagong to Strengthen Collaboration

Jan 09

0

On January 6, 2025, Team BdREN visited the University of Chittagong (CU) to foster collaboration and showcase its advanced services designed to enhance education and research. The visit, divided into three key sessions, underscored BdREN’s commitment to empowering academic institutions across Bangladesh.
The first session began with a welcome meeting with the CU leadership. Team BdREN, consisting of CEO Mr. Mohammad Tawrit, Dr. Mohammad Farooq Ali Tarafder FCMA, CAFO, Khandakar Rashedul Arefin, Manager (Data Center), Md. Ariful Islam, Manager (Data and Transmission) and Abu Naser Md. Nafew, Network Engineer engaged in a meet-and-greet with Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Muhammed Yeahia Akhter, Pro-Vice Chancellor (Academic) Professor Dr. Mohammed Shamim Uddin Khan, and Pro-Vice Chancellor (Administration) Professor Dr. Md. Kamal Uddin. The discussions highlighted BdREN’s dedication to enhancing CU’s digital and research infrastructure.
The second session, held in a packed auditorium, was the highlight of the visit. Faculty members and officials from CU actively participated in an engaging showcase of BdREN’s services. The program, titled
"Showcasing BdREN Services for CU Faculty,"
was organized by CU’s Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) and held in the Senate Room of Dr. A.R. Mallik Bhaban. The event was graced by CU Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Muhammed Yeahia Akhter as the “Chief Guest”, with Pro-Vice Chancellor (Academic) Professor Dr. Mohammed Shamim Uddin Khan, Pro-Vice Chancellor (Administration) Professor Dr. Md. Kamal Uddin, as “Special Guests” and BdREN CEO Mr. Mohammad Tawrit as “Guest of Honour”. The program was chaired by IQAC Director Professor Dr. Mohammad Mosharraf Hossain. During this session, Vice-Chancellor Professor Yeahia praised BdREN’s significant contributions to the nation’s educational and research infrastructure, particularly during the pandemic. He expressed optimism that CU could benefit substantially from BdREN’s services to enhance research and learning capabilities, thereby strengthening its position in global rankings. Pro-Vice Chancellor (Administration) Professor Dr. Md. Kamal Uddin also commended BdREN’s services, urging CU’s faculty and students to fully utilize the available opportunities to advance education, research, and innovation.
Once the formal inauguration of the program was over, BdREN Team showcased its range of services through impactful presentations from Manager (Data Center) Khandakar Rashedul Arefin who demonstrated on “BdREN Services". After that Network Engineer Abu Naser Md. Nafew came up with his presentation on "Implementation of Value-Added Services through AI." The participants showed high interest in the provided solutions especially on High-Performance Computing (HPC), Cloud Computing, AI-driven email automation, remote access to publisher services, and BdREN QuiGen - the automated Quiz Generation application. A lively open-floor discussion followed that reflected CU’s enthusiasm for collaboration with BdREN to explore innovative applications of these offerings. Prof. Dr. Shahadat Hossain, Additional Director (Quality Assurance), IQAC, coordinated and facilitated the program. He also ensured the program's smooth execution by overseeing all activities with precision and dedication.
The visit concluded with the inauguration of CU’s newly renovated Video Conferencing Room, facilitated by BdREN. The modern facility, equipped with state-of-the-art video conferencing cameras, sound systems and equipment, aims to enhance virtual collaboration and connectivity for CU’s faculty and students. The inauguration was officiated by CU Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Muhammed Yeahia Akhter, who connected live with UGC Member Professor Dr. Md. Saidur Rahman in BdREN VC Room, UGC Bhaban, Dhaka, marking a significant milestone in CU’s digital transformation.
BdREN’s visit to the University of Chittagong reaffirmed its commitment to transforming academic institutions across Bangladesh by offering cutting-edge digital infrastructure and fostering research collaboration. The active participation and enthusiasm from CU faculty and officials reflected the potential for a strong partnership to advance education and research excellence.

BdREN proudly co-sponsored
BitFest 2025
, a vibrant technology festival and competition organized by the
Department of CSE at KUET
. The event, held on January 3-4, 2025, on the KUET campus in Khulna, brought together students from KUET and other similar universities across Bangladesh. BdREN served as the
title sponsor of the Inter-University Programming Contest
, one of the festival's flagship events.
The festival was inaugurated by
Professor Dr. Mohammad Mashud
, Vice-Chancellor of KUET, with
CTO-BdREN Ekhlas Uddin Ahmed
joining the ceremony alongside prominent figures, including Pro-Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Sk. Shariful Alam, Faculty of EEE Dean Professor Dr. Md. Rafiqul Islam, and Director of Student Welfare Professor Dr. Mohammad Sultan Mahmud. The event was presided over by
Professor Dr. M.M.A. Hashem
, Head of the CSE Department, KUET. Themed
"Technology-Creativity-Collaboration,"

In his speech, CTO-BdREN highlighted
BdREN's role as the nation's primary research facilitator
, committed to advancing digitalization in education and research. He outlined BdREN's extensive range of services, including
eduroam, HPC, Cloud Services, Smart Classrooms, Federated e-Resource Access, and Campus Network Design
. Emphasizing BdREN's mission to create a
"Researchers' Heaven"
, he encouraged closer collaboration between academia and industry, particularly between KUET and BdREN, to strengthen research and education ecosystems.
CTO-BdREN concluded by commending the organizers of BitFest 2025 and reaffirming BdREN's dedication to empowering Bangladesh's academic community through cutting-edge digital services and solutions.

This milestone reflects BdREN's unwavering commitment to supporting the digital transformation of Bangladesh's higher education sector. By deploying cutting-edge caching infrastructure, we are empowering public universities to achieve their goals with greater efficiency and connectivity.
We extend our heartfelt appreciation to our technical team, partners, and stakeholders for their hard work and collaboration in bringing this project to fruition.
BdREN remains dedicated to driving innovation and enabling a smarter, connected academic community. Stay tuned for more breakthroughs!

BdREN Meets New ICT Director of Dhaka University to Strengthen Collaboration

Dec 18

0

On December 15, 2024, a team from the Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN), led by Chief Executive Officer Mohammad Tawrit, held a welcome meeting with
Professor Dr. Mosaddek Hossain Kamal
, the newly appointed ICT Director of Dhaka University (DU). The meeting, held at the Professor's office, was also attended by BdREN's Chief Technical Officer Ekhlas Uddin Ahmed and Manager of Data and Transmission Network Md. Ariful Islam.
The meeting centered on fostering greater cooperation between Dhaka University, the largest and most prestigious university in the country, and BdREN, the leading digitalization facilitator for education and research in Bangladesh. Highlighting BdREN's vision, encapsulated in its tagline
"Researchers' Heaven"
, CEO Mohammad Tawrit reaffirmed BdREN's commitment to providing state-of-the-art digital facilities to DU's research sector under the guidance and support of the
University Grants Commission (UGC)
.
Professor Dr. Mosaddek Hossain Kamal, a distinguished educationist and ICT expert, expressed his enthusiasm for transforming Dhaka University into a thriving hub for advanced research. He acknowledged BdREN's role in digitalizing Bangladesh's education landscape and assured his full support in leveraging BdREN's services to modernize DU's academic and research infrastructure.
The discussions began with an evaluation of
DU's internet bandwidth usage
and its subscription package with BdREN, along with the state of DU's existing network infrastructure. The conversation then expanded to cover a wide range of BdREN services and initiatives, including
High-Performance Computing (HPC)
, cloud services, local data center facilities, eduroam, Learning Management System (LMS), University Management System (UMS), Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI), federated access to journals and eBooks, certificate verification services, Zoom, and consultancy.
Professor Mosaddek, with his vast international experience, expressed interest in playing a consulting role to ensure the successful implementation of BdREN's projects, not just for Dhaka University but also for broader initiatives that align with BdREN's mission. His insights and expertise are expected to further strengthen the synergy between DU, BdREN, and UGC in achieving digital transformation goals.
The meeting concluded on a positive note, marked by mutual enthusiasm, optimism, and a shared vision for the future. Both parties expressed confidence in their collaboration's potential to advance research capabilities, technological innovation, and digital infrastructure for the benefit of Dhaka University and the broader academic community in Bangladesh.

BdREN and MIST Forge New Collaboration for Enhanced Digital Services and Research Support with Special Focus on LMS

Nov 11

0

A productive meeting took place between Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN) and the Military Institute of Science and Technology (MIST) on November 7, 2024, to explore new avenues for cooperation in digital and research services. Held in the MIST R&D Wing Conference Room in Dhaka, the session brought together key representatives from both organizations, including BdREN's CTO Ekhlas Uddin Ahmed and MIST's Director of R&D Brig. Gen. Mohammad Sajjad Hossain. The meeting underscored BdREN's commitment to providing Bangladeshi universities and research institutions with advanced digital solutions.

During the session, BdREN presented a comprehensive overview of its service offerings tailored for academic and research excellence. The services that were explained in the meeting included eduroam, high-speed internet, Zoom expansion, research bandwidth, high-performance computing (HPC), cloud services, disaster recovery, and federated access to e-resources. Special emphasis was placed on the Learning Management System (LMS), which has sparked keen interest from MIST as they look to streamline digital learning and resource management on campus. The discussion also delved into flexible options for Internet and related services, with MIST expressing their desire to receive HPC support, to be used for research purpose, at Free of charge from BdREN.

Looking ahead, MIST requested BdREN to prepare detailed quotations for various services, with a live demonstration of the LMS to be arranged after the return of the MIST Commandant on November 10. Both parties agreed this initial meeting is the start of a continued partnership, with more discussions planned to refine service offerings. BdREN reaffirmed its mission to support Bangladeshi educational institutions by creating a "Researchers' Heaven" through accessible, high-quality digital infrastructure, aligning with its role as a non-profit, government-owned trust serving the nation's academic and research community.

Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN) is pleased to announce its role as a Silver Sponsor at the 2nd International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (ICICT) 2024, held on October 21-22 at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET). Organized by BUET’s Institute of Information and Communication Technology (IICT) and technically co-sponsored by IEEE Bangladesh Section, the conference gathered a diverse group of experts, researchers, and professionals, making it a key event in the ICT calendar.
BdREN’s support as a Silver Sponsor highlights our dedication to fostering collaboration, innovation, and knowledge-sharing in the fields of information and communication technology. Our organization is committed to building a robust digital ecosystem in Bangladesh, connecting academia, research, and industry through seamless networking. This sponsorship aligns with our broader mission of promoting ICT advancement and enabling greater access to research and educational resources across the country.
As a valued participant in ICICT 2024, BdREN had the opportunity to showcase its initiatives, share its vision, and engage with thought leaders and stakeholders from around the world. Our presence at the conference also underscored our commitment to being a key player in Bangladesh’s journey towards digital transformation and enhanced connectivity.
BdREN remains committed to supporting initiatives that advance ICT research, innovation, and education. We are honored to have contributed to the success of ICICT 2024 and look forward to participating in more such events in the future, where we can continue to build partnerships, drive technological progress, and strengthen the ICT community both locally and globally.
For further details about ICICT 2024, including highlights from the event, please visit the official conference website:
https://icict.buet.ac.bd
.

11:00am-12:00pm [GMT+6]

Topic:
REN applications and collaborations in developing REN further

Chair:
Md. Saiful Islam, Professor, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET)

Panellists:
Takashi Tomine, Associate Senior Research Engineer
National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (ARENA-PAC)
Flávio Cardoso Neves, Chairman, ANC [Autoridade Nacional de Comunicações] Timor Leste
Mohammad Tawrit, Chief Executive Officer, BdREN

An online panel discussion was organised by “Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology” as a part of AI3/SOI Asia meeting to discuss research and education network infrastructure on October 24, 2024. SOI Asia (School on Internet Asia/read: soi-asia) Project was established in 2001 with the objective of achieving education collaborations between Southeast Asian universities on the internet, utilizing the infrastructure technology developed by AI³ Project. SOI Asia has been implementing human resource development programs in Asia in various fields, including information technology, security, marine technologies, environmental issues, cultural understandings, disaster management, and entrepreneurship. And from 2008, with cooperation with UNESCO, SOI Asia also contributes to the development of the next generation of global human resources, especially in science and technology.

Mohammad Tawrit in his presentation highlighted the application services BdREN has been providing for the community. Also, his presentation unfolded the collaboration among the NRENs both through bilateral and multilateral initiative in developing the infrastructure, applications, procurement, exchange of ideas and capacity development.

Takashi Tomine in his presentation highlighted the ARENA-PAC Network infrastructure detailing its connectivity with other NRENs.

Both the initiatives of ARENA-PAC and TEIN emerged as the infrastructure through which RENs are getting the benefit in exchanging the information. It was agreed by all concern that ARENA-PAC and TEIN should be integrated but they should play complementary roles for the beneficiary NRENs.

Also, the issue of increasing the REN bandwidth utilisation evolved through sharing of “High Performance Computing (HPC)” and other Application Services like File Sender.

The Chair concluded the session stressing on the following recommendations:
Connectivity for Collaboration
Capacity Building and Knowledge Transfer
Digital Libraries and Open Access Repository
Extending connectivity to remote and underserved areas
Disaster Response and Resilient Communications
High Performance Computing and Cloud Services
Cybersecurity for NRENs
Emerging Technologies and Future Opportunities

text:
BdREN Participates in 16th Asi@Connect Meeting in Seoul, South Korea

Oct 23

0

The 16th Asi@Connect Meeting was held in Seoul, South Korea, from October 16 to 18, 2024. The event featured a series of sessions, including the Governors' Meeting, Steering Committee Meetings, and Task Force Meetings. Prof. SMA Faiz, Chairperson-BdREN attended the meeting as  Governor, Asi@Connect project. Mohammad Tawrit, Chief Executive Officer-BdREN, and Dr. Mohammad Farooq Ali Tarafder FCMA, ACS, Chief Administrative and Fianance Officer-BdREN, participated in the meetings as resource person and steering committee member respectively.

Asi@Connect is the successor to TEIN4 (Trans-Eurasia Information Network) which supports 24 economies by providing a regional high-capacity internet backbone for research and education collaborations within the Asia-Pacific region. The network also connects the pan-European GÉANT network as well as academic and research networks in other global regions with high-bandwidth links.

This particular meeting was convened to address the issues related with the future of Asi@Connect project, especially focusing on the financing of the next phase, as the present phase is destined to expire on August 2025. During the event, BdREN’s CEO, Mohammad Tawrit, on behalf of the Task Force Team which comprised of representatives from different NRENs and TEINCC, presented the "Cost Share Model" for Asi@Connect Phase-2.

Threadbare discussions followed the presentation on the model and the figures were slightly revised based on the comments of the Governors to plug all the holes and to make it flawless. Finally, the meeting concluded with a voting for approval of the revised model. Almost all the participants voted in favor of the revised “Cost Sharing Model” with Japan-AP being the only exception which abstained from giving votes.

Second Security Awareness Community Workshop from Geant

Oct 21

0

We are cordially inviting our Bangladeshi Research and Education community to join this free workshop on
Second Security Awareness Community Workshop
from Geant. Here's an invitation from our fellow NREN Belnet:
Following the success of our first workshop at the GÉANT Security Days in April 2024, we are thrilled to invite you to the second meeting of the
GÉANT Security Awareness Community
which will take place online on 12 November.

We are delighted to welcome
Prof. Dr. Kristin Weber
, Vice President for Digitalisation and CIO at the Technical University Würzburg-Schweinfurt (THWS), as our keynote speaker. Prof. Weber will explore the four key behaviours in cyber security, introducing the COM-B model – a science-based framework that identifies essential components for behavioural change.

In interactive break-out sessions, participants will apply the COM-B model to practical security awareness scenarios, such as reporting malicious messages and safe authentication practices. The sessions will be moderated by members of the Subtask Awareness, ensuring a dynamic and collaborative learning environment.

To conclude, KU Leuven will share their security awareness programme 'e-mune', offering insights on how they built a culture of information security among staff and students.

This workshop is open to all security awareness professionals, whether you are just starting out or have years of experience. Please note that active participation is required during the break-out discussions.

Register here :
https://events.geant.org/event/1709/

Feel free to share this information with colleagues who might be interested.

Have you joined our cybersecurity awareness community? Not yet? You can do it today:
https://lists.geant.org/sympa/subscribe/securityawareness
For more information about our cybersecurity awareness initiatives, please visit
https://security.geant.org/awareness

We look forward to your participation!

Kind regards,
The Subtask Awareness

Davina Luyten
Product-Marketing • Belnet

On 30 September 2024, BdREN organized a "Workshop on IT Infrastructure" at Government Brajalal College, Khulna. Mohila College, Khulna, Daulatpur Day/Night College, Satkhira, Govt. PC College, Satkhira, Govt. Sundarban Adarsha College, Khulna, Satkhira Govt. College, Bagerhat, Satkhira Govt. text:
BdREN Expands eduroam Service to Multiple Airports, Enhancing Global Academic Connectivity

Sep 29

0

In a significant advancement for academic and research collaboration, Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN) has successfully expanded its eduroam service across multiple international airports in Bangladesh. Following the trailblazing launch of eduroam at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport (HSIA) – the first airport in South Asia to offer this service – eduroam is now made available in previously uncovered areas (CIP terminal, EBL Lounges, etc.) within HSIA, as well as at two new international airports in the country namely Osmani International Airport in Sylhet and Shah Amanat International Airport in Chittagong with effect from 10 September 2024.
A Pioneering Milestone for Academic Connectivity in Bangladesh
The initial launch of eduroam at HSIA on May 31, 2023, marked a groundbreaking moment for Bangladesh, establishing the country as a regional leader in academic connectivity. The service, which allows students, researchers, and faculty members to connect seamlessly to a global WiFi network, supports uninterrupted academic activities such as remote lectures, accessing research resources, and collaboration with peers. This development underscores Bangladesh's commitment to fostering education and research on an international scale.
Expanding Coverage and Accessibility
With the recent expansion, BdREN, in collaboration with Aamra Networks Limited and the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), has extended eduroam’s coverage to include airport lounges, previously uncovered WiFi areas, and EBL lounges at HSIA. Additionally, travelers passing through Sylhet and Chittagong can now benefit from the same high-speed, reliable connectivity.
BdREN’s efforts have now turned toward the next ambitious phase: implementing eduroam at local airports across Bangladesh. This will bring the same level of connectivity to a broader audience, enabling academic professionals to remain connected no matter where they travel within the country.
Looking Ahead: Local Airports in Focus
With the success at international hubs, BdREN aims to roll out eduroam services to local airports in Bangladesh, further extending the reach of this global education network. By creating a seamless, accessible digital environment, Bangladesh is poised to strengthen its role as a hub for research, education, and international collaboration.

BdREN Meets GSS in Malaysia for groundbreaking Software Development Collaboration

Sep 29

0

At BdREN, we’re always exploring new frontiers in innovation and partnership to enhance our service offerings. Recently, our leadership team embarked on an exciting journey to Malaysia to meet with Global Support Service (GSS), at the prestigious Malaysia Eco City during 12 September and 13 September 2024.

Our agenda

To discuss the development of a transformative software solution that will revolutionize the way we manage events, memberships and finances. The meeting was critical in laying the groundwork for a cutting-edge system designed to elevate organizational operations across multiple sectors.

The Vision for the Software

The project envisions a powerful, integrated platform with three key pillars:

1. Event Management System
– Streamlining the planning, coordination, and execution of events, from small workshops to large-scale conferences. This system will offer features like online registration, attendee tracking, scheduling, and real-time updates.

2. Membership Management Syste
m – A robust tool to help organizations manage their members efficiently. From registration to renewals, communication, and engagement tracking, the system will ensure a seamless experience for all users.

3. Finance Management System –
This component will be the backbone of financial operations. It will simplify budgeting, financial reporting, invoicing, and expense management, ensuring transparency and accountability for organizations.

A Milestone in Collaboration

Held at the iconic Malaysia Eco City, the meeting between BdREN and GSS marked a significant milestone in our journey towards creating this groundbreaking software solution. The modern surroundings of Eco City provided the perfect environment for innovation and collaboration. Representatives from both sides exchanged ideas, explored technological advancements, and brainstormed ways to address the unique challenges of our respective industries.

Throughout the discussions, it was clear that GSS shares our commitment to delivering exceptional digital solutions. Their expertise in developing scalable, secure, and user-friendly software perfectly complements our mission to bring world-class technology to organizations across Bangladesh.

What’s Next?

As we move forward, both BdREN and GSS are committed to working hand-in-hand to bring this project to life. Our teams are currently in the early stages of design and development, focusing on ensuring that the software meets the diverse needs of our users.

With a clear roadmap in place, we’re excited about the possibilities this collaboration will unlock. Whether it’s simplifying event planning, enhancing membership engagement, or improving financial transparency, this software solution is poised to make a lasting impact.

We look forward to sharing more updates as the project progresses, and we’re confident that this partnership with GSS will result in a system that not only meets but exceeds expectations. Stay tuned for more details as we continue on this exciting journey!

text:
BdREN Sends Participants to Malaysia for GenAI-Driven Curriculum Development Workshop

Sep 29

0

The
AP-GAINED: Asia Pacific - Generative AI Integration for NREN Enhancement and Development
project, funded Asia Pacific Network Information Center (APNIC) Foundation, spearheaded by Lanka Education and Research Network (LEARN) in collaboration with Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN) and Asia Pacific University (APU) Malaysia, aims to bridge the digital divide in National Research and Education Networks (NRENs) across lower-income regions. By offering tailored Generative AI (GenAI) training and resources, the project will empower NRENs with the skills and tools to enhance network operations, support research, and drive innovation in education, particularly for resource-constrained institutions.

As part of its commitment to advancing educational and network technology in Bangladesh,
BdREN (Bangladesh Research and Education Network)
recently dispatched three participants to Malaysia to attend a pivotal curriculum development program held from 16 September to 20 September 2024. The program is centered around integrating
Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI)
into innovative educational, administration and network management systems, under the "Training the Trainer (TTT)" model.

This initiative is led by the
AI for Innovative Design and Education (AIDE) project
, under the auspices of the
UNESCO Chair
for Harnessing Innovations in Technology to Support Teachers & Quality Learning at
Asia Pacific University (APU)
. In collaboration with AIDE, BdREN participants, along with trainees from
LEARN (Lanka Education and Research Network)
, received expert instruction from trainers at APU.

The workshop, held in Malaysia, marks the first step in a transformative journey for BdREN's engineers and administrative staffs. The training will focus on leveraging GenAI for administration and network optimization, streamlining network operations, monitoring, and enhancing system efficiencies. After the in-person segment, the curriculum development will continue online, with collaborative efforts from both BdREN and LEARN until the curriculum is ready for pilot implementation.

This opportunity reflects BdREN's dedication to equipping its personnel with cutting-edge skills and technologies that will propel the research and education network to new heights in Bangladesh.

text:
'Agreement' Signing Ceremony on Developing and Implementing Certificate Verification Portal at BUP by BdREN

Sep 26

0

The renowned Public University- BUP (Bangladesh University of Professionals) offered BdREN (Bangladesh Research and Education Network), sometime early this year (2024), to prepare an online Certificate Verification Portal which would allow concerned individuals or Institutes to verify various Certificates issued by BUP for its students. BdREN agreed and then developed this certification portal free of charge as a token of friendly gesture based on long term relationship between these two institutions- BUP and BdREN. The first phase of this portal is already in operation where concerned institutes or individuals will be able to verify Certificates issued by BUP through online web-based verification by putting Name and Registration number in the portal. The second phase of this certificate verification portal is also developed and ready for implementation where hardcopy Certificates will be verified through scanning a QR code imprinted on the Certificate. This will also be in Operation by BUP soon. In the third phase, BdREN will prepare a 'System' by which softcopy of the Certificates also can be verified, remotely. All these methods are based on fully encrypted communication and therefore 100% authenticity is ensured. Once adopted by all the universities in the country, this will hopefully usher a new era where there will be no more fake certificates to befool the world.

For Operation and Maintenance of this Certificate Verification Portal, an Agreement has been signed between BUP and BdREN on 24th of September, 2024 at BUP premises. This Agreement was signed by respected Treasurer of BUP, Air Commodore Md Reza Emdad Khan, ndc, psc, GD (P) and the Chief Executive Officer of BdREN, Mohammad Tawrit. Other distinguished delegates from both the parties, also were present in the Signing Ceremony.

0

From May 19-20, 2024, National University organized a series of four intensive workshops at National Academy for Education Management (NAEM), Dhaka, focusing on "Access to e-Resources to Enhance Academic and Research Excellence" for Teachers Honors and Masters Colleges under National University. The Librarian and one Faculty Member from each of the 120 colleges as well as Faculty Members of National University were present in the workshop for being trained about the knowhow of getting access to 197 emerald journals through federated access using Trust Integrity and Group Management for Education and Reseach Federation (TIGERFED)_being owned and managed by BdREN. BdREN provided all the technical support in making the event successful.
The opening session on May 19 and May 20 was graced by the presence of  Prof. Dr. Md. Mashiur Rahman, Honorable Vice-Chancellor of National University, who inaugurated the workshops, while Prof. Dr. Mitul Nasiruddin conducted each of the workshops with his usual flamboyance and style.
Renowned Deans and Professors from National University were present in each of the workshops throughout the two-day rigorous event. Mohammad Tawrit, CEO of BdREN, were also present on behalf of BdREN.
Abu Naser Md. Nafew, an experienced Network Engineer at BdREN, conducted the workshops successfully as it was vindicated through collection of feedbacks after each of the workshop sessions. Jamilur Rahman and Shamim Ahmed, two network engineers from BdREN, assisted Nafew in orchestrating the hands-on activities. Md. Atiqur Rahman, Data Technician, BdREN assisted in setting up the laboratory facilities and the video conferencing setup.

The opening session on May 19 featured Prof. Dr. Md. Mashiur Rahman, Honorable Vice-Chancellor of National University, who inaugurated the event, while Mohammad Tawrit, CEO of BdREN, welcomed the attendees.
Throughout the workshops, participants engaged in engrossing training, lively discussions, and hands-on exercises to master e-Book and e-Journal access via TIGERfed. The collaborative atmosphere and exchange of best practices enriched the learning experience, equipping attendees to apply their new skills in their academic institutions.
The training was held in TTT (Train The Trainer) format with the notion that all these college representatives will return back to their premises and will try to organize similar workshops to ventilate their knowledge among the college faculty members. At the end CEO, BdREN expressed his resolve to arrange accesses to other journals in phases provided effective outcome is observed out of the taken initiative.

Echoing the organizer all the attendees pledged that they would return back to their colleges and would try to disseminate their earned knowledge among the fellow faculty members.

BdREN Partners with APAN to Develop Multilingual FileSender Application

Mar 19

0

In a significant collaboration aimed at facilitating seamless data sharing among researchers and educationalists, the Bangladesh Research and Education Network (BdREN) joined forces with the Asia Pacific Advanced Network (APAN) to develop a groundbreaking application called FileSender. The project, funded by Asi@Connect under its “Targeted Call” initiative, seeks to address the growing need for large file-sharing solutions with efficiency, comfort and due effectiveness in the academic and research community.
Recognizing the growing need for efficient data sharing among academic communities, the heart of this project is the creation of FileSender, a web portal designed to streamline the process of sharing larger files of varying sizes among users.
Moreover, acknowledging the diverse linguistic landscape of the Asia Pacific region, FileSender is able to translate the portal into over 20 languages, ensuring accessibility and usability for a wide range of users.This multilingual approach ensures that users from diverse backgrounds can utilize the platform with ease, fostering greater collaboration and knowledge exchange on a global scale.
A pivotal moment in this endeavor came with the signing of a contract between APAN and BdRENsolidifying their partnership and commitment to delivering FileSender to the academic community. The contract was signed by the APAN Chair, and Mohammad Tawrit, CEO, BdREN on behalf of Bangladesh Research and Education Network.
This contract signifies a shared vision of designing and building the application leveraging on BdREN’s expertise in Software Development, Data Center and Network Infrastructure with the assistance from APAN Secretariat to drive positive changes and advancements in research and education.
With the support of Asi@Connect and the expertise of both BdREN and APAN, FileSender is a cornerstone tool for researchers and academicians in the Asia Pacific region. The community is looking forward to the positive impacts of FileSender Application on knowledge exchange and collaboration within the academic community.
